title: Machine Learning for Spoofing and Layering Detection in Real-Time Market Surveillance: A Framework and a Semi-Synthetic Order-Book Benchmark
content: Spoofing and layering, in which orders are placed without intent to execute and canceled after influencing prices or visible liquidity, threaten market integrity, and fixed-threshold surveillance rules struggle to separate them from legitimate high-frequency trading. This paper proposes a machine learning framework for real-time spoofing and layering sur-veillance. The framework combines order-level, cancellation, trader-level, order-book, and temporal features; compares rule-based, supervised, ensemble, sequential, and anomaly-detection models; and specifies performance measures including precision, recall, false-alert rate, latency, and explainability. Because labeled spoofing data are not public, the evaluation protocol is exercised on a semi-synthetic benchmark: 183 hours of real BTC-USD order-book snapshots from a public exchange feed, with injected and labeled spoofing episodes. On a chronological test period, supervised models improved only modestly on a rule-based baseline (F1-score about 0.14 versus 0.10) and with low precision (at most about 0.12, against a base rate of about 0.03). Ensemble models did not outperform logistic regression, and detection depended strongly on episode intensity, from 21% to 45% of low-intensity episodes to 76% to 87% of high-intensity episodes. The results show that the protocol can be executed and give a first reference point, not evidence of operational readiness.
